name: Permanent residence permit (incl. EU long-term resident status)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 continuous years of legal residence on a non-temporary residence purpose.

value.note: excl. holiday allowance; €1,766.77 incl. holiday allowance — IND publishes both framings for this specific requirement

requirements.blocker_text: This requires independent and sustainable income of at least €1,635.90/month (excl. holiday allowance, 2026 figure).
requirements.fix_path: Ensure income meets the required threshold at time of application.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires having passed the civic integration exam (inburgering) at A2 level, unless exempt (EU/EEA/Swiss nationals need no integration exam).
requirements.fix_path: Book and pass the civic integration exam at A2.

evidence_required.document: Civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam certificate at A2 (unless exempt)
Income evidence meeting the required amount

notes: Netherlands' ILR/Niederlassungserlaubnis-equivalent hub route, same structural role as uk_ilr and de_niederlassungserlaubnis — one route most feeder routes resolve through. Two parallel legal types exist (national permanent residence permit and EU long-term resident permit), which IND checks automatically for the applicant — modeled here as a single route since the practical qualifying conditions and outcome are the same, with the EU long-term variant's main added value (easier intra-EU mobility) not separately captured, a scope decision. LANGUAGE LEVEL FLAGGED AS GENUINELY CONDITIONAL, not a simple constant: A2 remains the operative level in 2026 for most applicants, but expats who obtained their Dutch BSN after 1 January 2022 and are pursuing PR without naturalising may face a B1 requirement under the Wet inburgering 2021, depending on individual timeline — this route encodes the more common A2 case and flags the B1 sub-case honestly rather than silently picking one. Fee €254 adult / €85 for EU/EEA/Swiss nationals (who also skip the integration exam entirely) confirmed via IND. Income requirement is stated with BOTH holiday-allowance conventions by IND itself (€1,635.90 excl. / €1,766.77 incl.) — genuinely unusual, most other Dutch routes in this dataset use only one convention consistently.
